title: A simple and effective heat induced antigen retrieval method
author: K.R., Jones, et al.

steps.title: Prepare tissue sections on slides
steps.instruction: Collect male Sprague‑Dawley rat tissues, fix in 10 % neutral buffered formalin, embed in paraffin, cut sections 4–5 µm thick and mount on HistoGrip‑coated glass slides; dry slides on a slide warmer at 60 °C before further processing.

steps.title: Deparaffinise and rehydrate slides
steps.instruction: Deparaffinise the mounted sections and rehydrate them through graded alcohols to water, then keep the slides in a retrieval buffer of either sodium citrate (pH 6.0) or Tris‑EDTA (pH 9.0).

steps.title: Prepare slide pairs with paperclip
steps.instruction: For each tissue slide, place a plain glass slide on top, overlapping only one end; clip the overlapped end with a 2 in (≈5 cm) U‑shaped paperclip, leaving a small gap so buffer can reach the tissue and the slides are not jammed; shift the clipped end slightly clockwise to ease later removal.

substeps.instruction: Lay a plain slide over the tissue slide, overlapping one end only.
Clip the overlapped end with a 2‑inch U‑paperclip.
Ensure a narrow space remains for buffer contact and slide removal.

steps.title: Boil slides for antigen retrieval
steps.instruction: Place each slide pair into a beaker or water‑bath containing the chosen buffer (sodium citrate pH 6.0 or Tris‑EDTA pH 9.0) optionally supplemented with 0.05 % Tween 20; heat the bath to 95–100 °C and maintain boiling for 15 min (optimal 10–20 min for many antibodies, up to 30 min possible without damage).

substeps.instruction: Add buffer (citrate pH 6.0 or Tris‑EDTA pH 9.0, 0.05 % Tween 20) to a beaker or water bath.
Raise temperature to 95–100 °C and boil for 15 min (adjust 10–20 min as needed).

steps.title: Cool slides and remove clips
steps.instruction: Transfer the boiled slides to a vessel of tap water and let them cool for 10 min; while the slides are still in cold water, carefully remove the paperclips.

substeps.instruction: Move slides to tap‑water bath for 10 min cooling.
Remove the paperclips while slides are cold.

steps.title: Perform ABC immunostaining
steps.instruction: Carry out standard avidin‑biotin complex (ABC) staining: incubate sections with primary antibody for 1 h at room temperature, then with secondary antibody for 30 min–1 h at room temperature; pre‑incubate biotinylated HRP with free avidin for ~15 min, add this mixture to the tissue and incubate 30 min; develop with DAB chromogen and counterstain with hematoxylin.

substeps.instruction: Apply HRP‑avidin mix to tissue: 30 min.
Develop with DAB, then counterstain with hematoxylin.

description: Antigen retrieval is an important step in immunohistochemistry staining. The simple technique of boiling formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) tissue sections in water has played a major role in extending the reach and use of immunohistochemistry [1]. However, direct boiling of tissues in buffer often results in the damage of tissues or falling off tissues from the slide. Several reasons such as insufficient fixation, improper sectioning and drying, poor adherence and even uncleaned slides have been reported to contribute to the issue of falling off or detachment of tissues from slide [2], [3], [4], [5]. Even after taking care of above factors, the sections often tend to detach from adherent coated slides while boiling. In this paper, we present an additional step to the standard heat induced epitome retrieval (HIER) of tissues by which the damage or detachment of tissue from the slide while boiling can be prevented. In the present study, we have performed IHC staining with several antibodies with and without the additional step in the standard protocol. We found that the direct boiling without covering slides often resulted in loss of tissue from the slide. Additional step has always given the best results. Tissues were intact on the slide for further processing which improved the quality of staining by preventing damage or detachment of tissues from the slides. The comparisons of tissue morphology after directly boiling in buffer with and without slide clipping are given in Fig. 2 (qualitative) and Fig. 3 (quantitative). This simple additional step is also safe and economical. Protease digestion was the first method used to counteract the antigen masking effects of formalin fixation. However, since the advent of heat induced epitope retrieval (HIER) techniques, proteases play a much smaller role in most IHC laboratories [6]. Microwave ovens are also used for HIER.
